entity.name: Intelligence Cubed i³
entity.description:
Intelligence Cubed is building intelligence infrastructure that helps companies move from prompt-wrapper AI products to owned, fine-tuned model systems.

Most enterprise AI products today rely on generic foundation model APIs and prompt engineering, which makes it difficult for companies to own their model behavior, preserve domain expertise, reduce inference cost, or continuously improve from real user interactions. Intelligence Cubed solves this by turning product usage data into proprietary training assets and enabling companies to fine-tune, evaluate, deploy, and improve their own models over time.

Our platform helps teams collect, clean, label, approve, version, and evaluate high-quality training data from conversations, workflows, expert edits, user feedback, and business outcomes. Companies can then fine-tune owned models from approved behavior data, compare model versions, measure quality, latency, cost, and brand consistency, and deploy the best-performing models into production.

Beyond fine-tuning, Intelligence Cubed provides the evaluation, routing, deployment, and feedback-loop infrastructure needed to operate models continuously. We believe the future of enterprise AI will not be defined by static prompts or isolated APIs, but by companies that build compounding model advantages through proprietary data, fine-tuned behavior, and continuous improvement.

HOW TO SIGN UP 

Step 1: Registration 
Each Buyer (Company) can sign up and create an account by filling a form with general information such as login details and company details.

Step 2: Uploading/Searching for products 
Users can upload and display a product of their interest, add full description and specifications and share a relevant video from YouTube or Vimeo. Each Buyer can share its product info with Buyers from other countries.
Each member can also apply a user filter that restricts access to their displayed data, based on users region.

Step 3: Setting display features
Users can set an offer validity period which means that their product will be on display for a certain period of time.

BENEFITS

•	Small companies are able to participate in the production of a product by paying an extra percentage of product’s price to large companies. This constitutes a benefit for both companies, as small ones are able to purchase the desired order quantity at a lower price than the original quoted and at the same time large enterprises can buy the product at a more competitive price because of the increase in order quantity.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

Product managers, founders, and CX leaders deal with customer feedback scattered across app store reviews, support tickets, surveys, call transcripts, and chat logs. Most of it never gets read. You define what to look for. No rigid taxonomies or manual tagging.

Metricsense turns feedback into decisions, not dashboards full of charts nobody acts on.

entity.name: Metricsense.ai
entity.description:
Metricsense is a feedback intelligence platform that helps product teams stop guessing what to build.

Product managers, founders, and CX leaders deal with customer feedback scattered across app store reviews, support tickets, surveys, call transcripts, and chat logs. Most of it never gets read. The insights that could shape better product decisions sit buried in thousands of unstructured messages nobody has time to tag, sort, or analyze.

Metricsense connects all your feedback sources into one place and lets you ask questions in plain English. Instead of filtering through pre-built categories, you write natural language prompts like "What are the top onboarding complaints from enterprise accounts ?" and get structured, evidence-backed answers in minutes. Every insight links back to the raw customer quote so you can verify what the AI found.

What makes us different:

You define what to look for. No rigid taxonomies or manual tagging.
Every answer is traceable to the original feedback.
Custom alerts notify your team in Slack or email when metrics cross thresholds.
Auto-generated PRDs turn feature requests and bug reports into actionable specs, backed by real customer evidence.
We support CSV uploads, App Store and Google Play integrations, and real-time data feeds. Analysis runs on configurable AI models with customizable dimensions, dashboards, and drill-down into individual conversations.

Metricsense turns feedback into decisions, not dashboards full of charts nobody acts on.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:

    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).

    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.

    or keyword is not enough.

    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

entity.name: Intelligence Cubed i³
entity.description:
Intelligence Cubed is building intelligence infrastructure that helps companies move from prompt-wrapper AI products to owned, fine-tuned model systems.

Most enterprise AI products today rely on generic foundation model APIs and prompt engineering, which makes it difficult for companies to own their model behavior, preserve domain expertise, reduce inference cost, or continuously improve from real user interactions. Intelligence Cubed solves this by turning product usage data into proprietary training assets and enabling companies to fine-tune, evaluate, deploy, and improve their own models over time.

Our platform helps teams collect, clean, label, approve, version, and evaluate high-quality training data from conversations, workflows, expert edits, user feedback, and business outcomes. Companies can then fine-tune owned models from approved behavior data, compare model versions, measure quality, latency, cost, and brand consistency, and deploy the best-performing models into production.

Beyond fine-tuning, Intelligence Cubed provides the evaluation, routing, deployment, and feedback-loop infrastructure needed to operate models continuously. We believe the future of enterprise AI will not be defined by static prompts or isolated APIs, but by companies that build compounding model advantages through proprietary data, fine-tuned behavior, and continuous improvement.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.
